learning: Iteration 4 (5 sensors at 1.5 cm pitch) is the reference: s-bend 0.155, oval 0.11, slalom 0.1075, one line loss per run. Iterations 2 and 5 at 2 cm pitch both gave s-bend 0.04. This race tests whether a 1 cm pitch restores s-bend progress. Watch steering_oscillation, because more sensors could make the signal noisier, and check whether rms_error stays near 0.03, which would point to a motor-mismatch offset.
notes: Seven 16 mm sensors at 1 cm pitch across +/-3 cm, 4 cm lead, weights x/0.015 to match the iteration 4 slope. Gains and speed unchanged from iteration 4 so the pitch is the only geometry change.
rationale:
The Builder's proposal is a single-variable test from the iteration 4 reference (+/-3 cm span, 4 cm lead, 16 mm footprints, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius, 0.18 x 0.12 m body). Only the sensor pitch changes, from 1.5 cm (5 sensors) to 1 cm (7 sensors). The evidence supports this test. Iteration 4 gave s-bend progress 0.155, oval 0.11 and score 51.12. Iterations 2 and 5 both used a 2 cm pitch and both collapsed s-bend progress to 0.04. Iteration 3 used a 2 cm lead and also collapsed to 0.04, so the lead below 4 cm is harmful as well. Iteration 0 used 1 cm pitch and did not collapse (s-bend 0.15). That makes pitch a plausible cause, though iteration 5 changed span too, so it is not isolated.

Controller: the weights are rescaled to x/0.015, which gives [-2, -1.333, -0.667, 0, 0.667, 1.333, 2]. This keeps the same signal slope as iteration 4, where x = 0.015 m mapped to weight 1, so kp 3.0 carries over unchanged. Because the signal is a reading-weighted average, adding sensors at the same slope should not change the scale. kd stays at 0.1 and ki at 0, so the only controller change is the weight vector for the new sensor count. base_speed 1.6 and line_loss 'last_direction' are unchanged. Expected result, not measured: s-bend progress at or above 0.155, oval at or above 0.11, and line losses at or below 1 per run.
